newsitem.title: MONACO: OLYMPICS-FEDERATIONS SEEK MORE MONEY FROM OLYMPICS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-FEDERATIONS SEEK MORE MONEY FROM OLYMPICS.

text.p: International sports officials are still battling with Olympic chiefs for a bigger share of huge Games profits.

Primo Nebiolo, president of ASOIF which represents international sports federations at the Summer Games, said on Thursday that he had yet to reach his goal of receiving a larger slice of the revenue from the International Olympic Committee.

After a meeting with the IOC, Nebiolo, also head of the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF), said he would wait until IOC chief Juan Antonio Samaranch had finished his campaign for re-election in September before continuing the negotiations.

"Starting from Atlanta we have been discussing with the IOC about receiving money not only for TV revenue but from revenue going to the IOC for the Games from the top programme of sponsors," Nebiolo said.
"We also are discussing the possibility of each (international sports) federation receiving one percent of the tickets available from the venues where their sport is being held (at the Games)."

The money made by the biggest sporting event in the world is massive. The IOC recently signed a television deal with the American network NBC worth more than $2 billion. The contract which the IOC has with its leading sponsors is worth around $400 million over four years.

Officials said the international sporting federations in ASOIF received about $86 million from last year's Atlanta Games. Some of the money came from the marketing of the Games and some from television.
